security_spec.violation_condition: The host kernel (acting as untrusted domain manager) modifies the shared memory at connection_data_addr_out or transcript_data_addr_out between the TSM's write and the TVM's consumption, or the kernel supplies a tampered/replayed transcript via sbi_covh_get_device_connection_transcript() that the TSM fails to verify against its digest map before returning to the TVM
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: shared memory region passed to SBI CoVE-IO ABI without post-read integrity verification; consumption of device connection transcript data from shared pages without validating against TSM-attested digest; TOCTOU on 4KB-aligned shared buffers between sbi_covh_connect_device/sbi_covh_get_device_connection_transcript and sbi_covg_get_device_connection_transcript
security_spec.summary: Untrusted host kernel controls shared memory pages used for device connection transcript exchange between TSM and TVM; without kernel-side enforcement that transcript data is consumed atomically with TSM digest verification, the host can tamper with device identity/measurement data to trick a TVM into accepting a compromised or impersonated device into its TCB

findings.finding: Function does not exist in this kernel tree. The CoVE-IO SBI extension (sbi_covh_connect_device, sbi_covh_spdm_data, sbi_covh_get_device_connection_transcript, sbi_covg_get_device_connection_transcript) is defined in the RISC-V AP-TEE-IO specification but has no kernel implementation. No shared-memory TOCTOU or transcript-verification vulnerability can exist in code that hasn't been written.

Generic TSM registration infrastructure (Intel x86-focused CoCo subsystem). No RISC-V CoVE-IO SBI calls are made. Provides class-device registration for TEE Security Managers. Does not handle shared memory buffers, transcripts, or SPDM data — those are the responsibility of arch-specific SBI glue that does not exist in this tree.

PCI TSM ops interface (connect, bind, guest_req) for TDISP/SPDM. No RISC-V CoVE-IO ABI integration. When a RISC-V CoVE-IO backend is eventually implemented through this framework, the security spec's TOCTOU concerns will apply to the guest_req() path where TVM data crosses the host/guest boundary via sockptr_t buffers.
